title: Smooth sections give continuous test-density pairings
statement: Let $N$ be a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth real manifold without boundary [def-sfb-smooth-real-manifold], and $E\to N$ a smooth finite-rank real vector bundle [def-sfb-smooth-real-vector-bundle]. Form $E^*$, $\mathrm{Dens}_N$ and $E^*\otimes\mathrm{Dens}_N$ by [def-sfb-smooth-dual-bundle], [def-sfb-smooth-density-line] and [def-sfb-smooth-tensor-bundle]. Give $\mathcal T(E)=\Gamma_c^\infty(E^*\otimes\mathrm{Dens}_N)$ the compact smooth section topology of [def-sfb-compact-smooth-section-topology]. For every $s\in\Gamma^\infty(E)$ [def-sfb-smooth-bundle-sections] and every finite chart cover $\mathcal A$ with subordinate smooth partition $\rho$ as in [def-sfb-smooth-density-integral], the formula $L_s(\phi)=J_{\mathcal A,\rho}(\phi(s))$ defines a continuous real-linear functional on $\mathcal T(E)$. Here $\phi(s)$ is fibrewise contraction, sending $(\lambda\otimes\eta,s(x))$ to $\lambda(s(x))\eta$, extended linearly.

source.place: WANTED locally: inherited Part I §3.A–3.B, printed pp.11–13 (page attribution inherited, not independently verified). Agent-stated real density convention, supporting continuity of the smooth-section embedding into distributions. No claim of reading this unavailable source.

proof.text: In a chart with a smooth frame $e_a$ of $E$, write $s=\sum_a s_a e_a$ and $\phi=\sum_a\phi_a e^a\otimes|dz|$. The contraction has coefficient $\sum_a\phi_a s_a$. Evaluation on the dual and the bilinearity relations of the tensor product show this is well defined fibrewise; changing frames cancels the inverse dual matrix with the vector matrix, and changing density generators multiplies it by exactly the density transition factor. The finite sum of products of smooth coefficient functions is smooth, so $\phi(s)$ is a smooth density. Pointwise, $(a\phi+b\psi)(s)=a\phi(s)+b\psi(s)$. The linearity clause of [lem-sfb-density-integral-choice-independent] now proves that $L_s$ is real-linear for the specified $\mathcal A,\rho$.

source.place: Supporting analytic prerequisite in the inherited chain below (3); agent proof of the distributional section pairing. Demailly source requested in report; no analytic proof is claimed in this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: Choose smooth chart neighbourhoods on which $E$ has a smooth frame, by intersecting a manifold chart with a bundle trivializing neighbourhood and restricting both. They cover $N$; compactness supplies a finite subcover $(y_j:W_j\to V_j)_{j\in H}$ with frames $e_j$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subordinate-partition] with the closed set $N$ and this finite cover to obtain $0\leq\theta_j\leq1$, $\sum_j\theta_j=1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\theta_j\subseteq W_j$. Its hypotheses hold: $N$ is Hausdorff, smooth, finite-dimensional, and compact implies sigma-compact (the countable compact cover may be constant $N$). Put $K_j=y_j(\operatorname{supp}\theta_j)\subseteq V_j$. The support is closed in compact $N$, hence compact: an open cover of it extends to one of $N$ by adding its complement. Its continuous chart image is compact: pull an open cover back and take a finite subcover. Thus each $K_j$ is compact; empty supports may be retained.

source.place: Supporting analytic prerequisite in the inherited chain below (3); agent proof of the distributional section pairing. Demailly source requested in report; no analytic proof is claimed in this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: Let $s_j:V_j\to\mathbf R^q$ and $\phi_j:V_j\to\mathbf R^q$ be the coefficients in $e_j$ and $e_j^*\otimes|dy_j|$, respectively. Extend $s_j$ arbitrarily, for example by zero, outside $V_j$; it remains continuous on $K_j$. By [lem-sfb-compact-continuous-norm-bound], choose $B_j\geq0$ with $\|s_j(z)\|\leq B_j$ on $K_j$ (replace a returned bound by its maximum with zero). By [def-sfb-compact-smooth-section-topology], $p_j(\phi)=\sup_{K_j}\|\phi_j\|$ is one of the generating order-zero seminorms. For $z\in K_j$, the elementary inequalities $|v_a|\leq\|v\|$ and $|\sum_a t_a|\leq\sum_a|t_a|$ give $|\sum_{a=1}^q\phi_{j,a}(z)s_{j,a}(z)|\leq qB_jp_j(\phi)$. The sum is zero if $q=0$, and the empty-supremum convention handles $K_j=\varnothing$.

source.place: Supporting analytic prerequisite in the inherited chain below (3); agent proof of the distributional section pairing. Demailly source requested in report; no analytic proof is claimed in this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: For the chart cover $\mathcal B=(y_j)$ and partition $\theta$, the definition of $J_{\mathcal B,\theta}$ makes its $j$th integrand $h_j$ the zero extension of $(\theta_j\circ y_j^{-1})\sum_a\phi_{j,a}s_{j,a}$. It vanishes outside $K_j$ and satisfies $|h_j|\leq qB_jp_j(\phi)$ on $K_j$. Euclidean Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets, so [lem-sfb-real-compact-supported-integral-bound] gives $|\int h_j|\leq C_jp_j(\phi)$, where $C_j=qB_j\operatorname{vol}(K_j)\geq0$ is finite and independent of $\phi$. Sum the finite inequalities and apply the choice-independence clause of [lem-sfb-density-integral-choice-independent] to the smooth density $\phi(s)$: $$|L_s(\phi)|=|J_{\mathcal B,\theta}(\phi(s))|\leq\sum_{j\in H}C_jp_j(\phi).$$ Both chart families and partitions meet that lemma's hypotheses; this is why the originally specified charts need not trivialize $E$.

source.place: Supporting analytic prerequisite in the inherited chain below (3); agent proof of the distributional section pairing. Demailly source requested in report; no analytic proof is claimed in this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: For $\epsilon>0$ put $\delta=\epsilon/(1+\sum_j C_j)>0$. The finite intersection $U=\bigcap_j\{\phi:p_j(\phi)<\delta\}$ is a zero neighbourhood by [def-sfb-compact-smooth-section-topology]. For $\phi\in U$ the preceding bound gives $|L_s(\phi)|\leq\delta\sum_j C_j<\epsilon$. At any $\phi_0$, the translate $\phi_0+U$ is a neighbourhood, and real-linearity gives $|L_s(\phi_0+\phi)-L_s(\phi_0)|=|L_s(\phi)|<\epsilon$. This proves continuity directly. If $H$ is empty the estimate is zero and $U$ is the entire test space. For $N=\varnothing$ the original integral is the empty zero sum; $q=0$ also gives the zero functional. When $m=0$, the same argument uses finite-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbf R^0$ and its usual Lebesgue measure; neither cited analytic bound requires positive dimension.
